Scaling it up a bit from a real snail for a whimsical fairy-tale proportion, roughly cottage-sized relative to the snail's body.

Now I'm planning the snail's skeleton: a body length around 0.7-0.8m with the shell around 0.45m tall, laying out a spine as a curved path from tail to head using a few control points, then figuring out whether to use one continuous spine chain with a hips root joint or split it into separate tail and neck/head chains.

Then I need a head joint parented to the front tip, with a jaw joint for the lower jaw, plus a small snail mouth with separate upper and lower lips. For eyestalks and lower feelers I'll chain them off the head as tentacle-role parts, mirrored to the left side. Finally I'm sweeping the body mesh along the back/core/front bones with a tapered radius profile, thin at the tail tip, widening at mid-body, then narrowing again toward the neck.

Still shaping the body radii...

Adding more path points through the tail and head, then computing segment lengths to figure out where the arm's joint should sit along the curve—settling on positioning the core near the midpoint around P2.

Now I'm defining the radius profile at each point along the body, checking that each matches the path's y-coordinate closely enough to stay within the tolerance, and rounding off the tail's cap.

Actually, to simplify orientation, I'll avoid aim-based rotation entirely and just use world axes with scaled sphere geometry for the head—placing its center slightly forward and down from the head joint, with scale values controlling width, height, and length directly.

For the jaw, I'll parent a smaller flattened ellipsoid to the head joint, positioned forward and below, to serve as the lower jaw, plus a thin dark mouth marking.

I'll build each eyestalk as a tapered tentacle chain of four joints using a catmull-rom curve, with a small sphere eye bulb at the tip textured with a storybook-style eye decal showing white sclera, black pupil, and highlight.
